text: The Patriots dominated the Pittsburgh Steelers 20-3 in their Week 2 home opener at Gillette Stadium, with TreVeyon Henderson punching in a touchdown and the defense establishing itself early through aggressive man coverage schemes, though film review of Drake Maye's performance revealed the question of whether the second-year quarterback can sustain the offensive rhythm that fueled last season's Super Bowl run. The victory came at a cost, as starting right guard Mike Onwenu suffered a broken right ankle that will likely sideline him moving forward, adding to what proved to be a banged-up afternoon for the Pats despite the convincing win. Head Coach Mike Vrabel's squad also made franchise history by becoming the first of the original AFL teams to reach 600 wins, a milestone that underscores New England's sustained excellence over decades, even as this particular iteration continues to find its offensive footing with Maye under center against top-tier defenses.
